channel.title: Two-Year CS Redesign :: CS Two Year Refactor
channel.description: This website presents the Department of Computer Science’s plans for a restructured foundational Computer Science core. This is a two-year course progression incorporating a spiral curricululum design approach that attempts to modernize and streamline core computer science learning, emphasize the development of systems thinking (including humanistic aspects and human interactions with computational systems). This two-year core will serve as a shared starting point for CS specialization degrees (Cybersecurity, AI) and is designed with community college transfer and service courses to other departments in mind.

item.title: Core Design
item.description: What the curriculum IS: the two-year core course sequence, the twelve threads (eight spirals, three lenses, one bounded practice) plus two cross-cutting norms, and the program overview.

item.title: Competency-Based Assessment
item.description: How the program assesses against the structure. Competencies belong to the program, not to individual courses; courses are evidence-generating contexts. Grades and competency status run as parallel tracks. This chapter is a stub — the principles below are established in the design log but not yet written up as full pages. To document: the program-vs-course competency model; the parallel grade/competency tracks; signature assessments (Code Archaeology, Data Investigation, Design Review, the Team Software Project, the System Integration Project); how evidence accumulates across blocks; how lens/thread competencies are assessed without dedicated courses; the role of reflection and retrospectives.

item.title: Pedagogical Approach
item.description: How the program teaches. The spiral method (ideas recur, each return deepening), practice-before-formal sequencing, the recurring developmental experiences (Read → Repair → … → Reflect), the disciplined use of AI, and the real institutional systems (signature applications) students learn against. This chapter’s principles are regenerated against the real course sequence (resources/reference/degree-maps/cs.md) as of 2026-07-15 — see resources/design-log.md for what changed and what’s still open. Concrete-before-general (e.g. CIS 220’s browser-as-mini-OS framing as an on-ramp to operating-system concepts) and depth-of-engagement as a load-control lever remain live principles, expressed throughout the pages below rather than as separate pages of their own.

item.title: Course Designs
item.description: The individual courses that instantiate the structure.

item.title: Specializations
item.description: The upper-division degrees built on the identical common core. Every degree = the two-year core + a degree-specific upper division. Each specialization is on-ramped by particular core threads.

item.title: Analyses
item.description: How the design satisfies external requirements: ABET accreditation mappings, the K-State degree replacement, and service-department mappings.
